novum_candidates.description: The Karadi are alien invaders from space who conquered Earth during World War III not to seize material resources but to feed parasitically on human emotional suffering. They deliberately outlaw medicine, suspend utilities, cultivate doubt, and encourage displays of emotion, engineering a totalizing regime of despair as a form of sustenance ('sadistic fungi'). This governs the entire storyworld and the psychological logic of the narrative.

novelty.rationale: The arrival of the Karadi from space and their totalizing occupation constitutes a world-altering difference from the empirical norm: civilization is reduced to rubble, utilities suspended, medicine outlawed, and short-wave listening is punishable by death. The premise of an occupying power that feeds on human emotion rather than resources is a totalizing transformation of the story universe.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The story develops a coherent immanent, nonsupernatural logic: the Karadi possess invincible weapons that disarmed all armies, and they sustain an occupation whose every policy (outlawing medicine, suspending utilities, encouraging emotional display, planting quislings) is systematically explained as a means to cultivate the suffering they feed on. The cat-conditioning analogy provides an internally consistent behavioral rationale. Present-day buildability is not required; the imaginary social-biological logic is coherent.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The Karadi occupation determines the overriding narrative logic. Every plot element—Freddie's conscription and reported death, the culture of doubt, the short-wave subversion, and Mr. Friedlander's ultimate betrayal of his neighbors—flows directly from the regime of engineered despair. The tragic ending, in which doubt drives Friedlander to inform, is the fulfillment of the novum's central mechanism.

novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: The reader is estranged by the contrast between remembered pre-invasion abundance (steak, chicken, lobster) and present turnip-water poverty, and by the inversion of a conqueror who wants emotional suffering rather than resources, dramatizing how a manufactured epistemic doubt corrodes human solidarity.

novum_candidates.description: Advanced 'dart-swift' Karadi aircraft piloted by conscripted humans against the last free human strongholds in the Rocky Mountains.

novelty.rationale: The aircraft and 'invincible weapons' are technologically superior to the empirical norm, but they are best understood as instruments of the broader occupation novum rather than a distinct world-altering difference in their own right.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The planes and weapons are presented as coherent alien technology but receive no independent systematic account beyond being 'invincible' and 'dart-swift'; they function as props of the occupation.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The aircraft is an incidental device. It provides the offstage occasion for Freddie's reported death but does not itself determine the narrative logic; the psychological regime of doubt does. It is subordinate to the occupation novum.

novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: The image of a father's son forced to pilot enemy aircraft against free humans estranges the reader through the perversion of familial and civic loyalty, but this serves the larger occupation theme rather than standing as an independent novum.
